profile.headline: Software Engineer at Google
profile.geoLocationName: New York, New York, United States
profile.summary:
Quantitative analyst and former computational astrophysicist. Strong background in analysis and visualization of large data sets.  Significant experience modeling complex phenomena using mathematical and computational methods. Excellent problem solving and written and oral communication skills. Strong focus on solving problems that have a direct impact on the success of the business 

Proficient in object-oriented programming and design patterns (C++, C#, Java) and functional programming (R and F#).  Familiar with the formal software development and testing process as a contributor to production software for financial derivatives pricing.  Experience with parallel and multithreaded programming.

Specialties: data analysis, mathematical modeling, software development, algorithms, scientific programming

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Nest Energy Intelligence team (2019 - present), Play Ads Quality team 2017 - 2019).

positions.title: Associate Principal
positions.description: Working to keep Google products safe from abuse.

positions.title: Quantitative Analyst
positions.description:
Currently a member of the eCommerce FX trading desk, a high frequency electronic market maker.  Analyzed large market and trade data sets in order to improve pricing and risk management algorithms.  Worked on various projects including P&L decomposition, client trading demand function, and analysis of microstructure noise in market FX rates.

Previously a member of Quantitative Strategies derivatives modeling team.  Contributed to Excel add-ins and spreadsheets for pricing of interest rate derivatives.  Developed database applications using a combination of SQL, Excel and .NET technologies to identify high-risk counterparties.

positions.title: Postdoctoral Fellow
positions.description:
Conducted an independent research program in computational cosmology, presented results at numerous international conferences, and published several articles in leading scientific journals including the following: 
 
• Analyzed a large cosmological simulation with a total data volume of over 20 terabytes and estimated the probability of finding high velocity “bullet” galaxies.  
Published in Hayashi, E. and White, S.D.M. (2006). How rare is the bullet cluster? Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, 370:L38-L41 (http://tinyurl.com/6sapcon).

• Produced detailed visualizations of the velocity fields of disk galaxies expected in currently favoured cosmological models.  
Published in Hayashi, E. and Navarro, J.F. (2006). Hiding cusps in cores: kinematics of disc galaxies in triaxial dark matter haloes. Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, 373:1117-1124 (http://tinyurl.com/cs3kcxl).

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description: Co-op work-study program work-term.  Performed laser-induced fluorescence experiments for the remote sensing research division as part of a collaboration with Agriculture Canada.

positions.description: Co-op work-study program work-term.  Developed hardware control software in LabView for use in high energy physics experiments.
